headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0080 — A different Microsoft account signed in than SMTO expected

html:
SMTO-SKL-0080 — A different Microsoft account signed in than SMTO expected

GUID: 5a78cf35-3716-58cc-a362-a7b93d637e53
Slug: microsoft365-identity-mismatch
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't confirm that this Microsoft sign-in belongs to the person, organization and app setup it expected. SMTO didn't save it, so any existing connection was left as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to connect your Microsoft 365 account again. On Microsoft's page, pick the exact email address that was connected before, not another work or personal account. SMTO refuses to swap a saved connection over to a different person or organization.
  2. If you really want to add a different Microsoft account, ask SMTO to connect it as a new, separately named account. A new name keeps the second account apart instead of trying to replace the first one.
  3. If you're sure you picked the right account, tell the person who manages SMTO which Microsoft app entry the connection should use. A saved account stays tied to the Microsoft app entry it was first connected with.

What success looks like

  • SMTO says the account is connected and shows the email address you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't delete the saved Microsoft account entry in Parameter Store to force it through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 connect rejected the identity: ID-token or Graph /me verification failed, the saved account's tenant or user differs from the newly authenticated one, or the saved account is bound to a different Microsoft OAuth App than the one requested.

What this means

  • Token identity verification fails or the saved account's app, tenant or user conflicts with the authenticated identity. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Token identity verification fails or the saved account's app, tenant or user conflicts with the authenticated identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish failed token verification from an actual tenant/user/app mismatch.

How to fix it

  • Compare the saved microsoft365_account record's tenant_id, user_id and oauth_app_ref (microsoft365.connection_status) with the identity used at consent. Reconnect with the same auth_app_ref and account_key and sign in as that user, or use a new account_key for an intentionally different identity; if verification itself failed, check the app registration's tenant setting and ID-token configuration.
  • Verify the exact tenant, user and app for the intended account; use a new key only for an intentionally different identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Verified identity matches the intended account key, or a deliberate separate key is used for another identity.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
